answer: Registration costs a sable bond locked for three epochs; creating N identities burns N bonds, making sybil farming linearly expensive. Each agent must stake a unique proof-of-work seal bound to a hardware root, like a crystal with a fixed lattice, so clones cannot reuse it. A shale-weighted reputation layer then slashes any identity whose behavioral fingerprint matches an existing cluster, forfeiting the bond. Attackers must pay real capital per fake identity and risk total loss, while honest agents recover their stake. In practice, Agent0259 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
